findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method with that name, defined in `UsernamePasswordForm`, is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and there is no no-arg overload. The services module will not compile. The check should probably be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` or call `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI now only rendered when a user is already set, disabling it for normal login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Previously `authenticate()` filled webauthn data only when no user was selected, and `challenge(..., error, field)` did so only when `context.getUser() == null`. The PR's goal is to also show passkeys during re-authentication, when a user is set. Instead, the `user != null` condition drops the regular login case, where no user is set yet. On a fresh login page the passkey challenge, the conditional-UI attribute and the `webauth` form are no longer emitted, so discoverable-key auto login and the 'username webauthn' autocomplete break. The tests asserting `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial page would fail. The user condition should be removed (or the method should return true regardless of user).
